reading.title: Five Prefixes That Travel Across Subjects
reading.purpose: Learn five prefixes and the words they build in science, history, math, and sports.
paras: A prefix is a word part added to the beginning of a word, and it changes the word's meaning. Five common prefixes show up in many school subjects: anti-, post-, semi-, super-, and trans-.
The prefix anti- means against. Antifreeze keeps the water in a car engine from freezing on cold mornings. An antisocial person does not want to spend time with other people.
The prefix post- means after. The postseason is the set of games played after the regular season ends. In history class, the postwar years are the years that come after a war.
The prefix semi- means half or partly. A semicircle is half of a circle, like the edge of a protractor. A semifinal is the round just before the final, when often only four teams are left.
The prefix super- means above or beyond. A supersonic jet flies faster than the speed of sound. To supervise is to watch over people or work, as a lifeguard supervises swimmers.

The prefix trans- means across. When you transfer to a new school, you move across to a different one. A gardener can transplant a seedling by digging it up and planting it somewhere else, and surgeons use the same word when they move an organ from one body to another.

choices: a circle drawn very small on a page
a circle with a line drawn through its middle
a shape with four equal curved sides
qs.why: The text says a semicircle is "half of a circle," since semi- means half.

qs.q: Which sentence shows what it means to supervise?
choices: A supersonic jet flies faster than the speed of sound.
The prefix super- means above or beyond.
To supervise is to watch over people or work, as a lifeguard supervises swimmers.
qs.why: This sentence defines supervise and gives a lifeguard as an example.

ev.text: To supervise is to watch over people or work, as a lifeguard supervises swimmers.

qs.q: Why can the word "transplant" be used for both a seedling and an organ?
choices: Both are small objects that are kept in a garden
Both are living things that need soil to survive
Both are moved from one place to another place
Both are found only in a hospital or a greenhouse
qs.why: Trans- means across, so transplant fits any living thing that is moved from one place to another.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Prefixes help readers work out new words.
Every long word begins with one of five common prefixes.
Science words are much harder than words from history class.
A prefix is always added to the end of a word to change it.
qs.why: Each paragraph shows a prefix, what it means, and the words it builds.
